solver.kind: blind AI solver (separate agent, answer-free packet, rubric v2)

flags: minor: key C states the author's later view of form ('form as part of its meaning'), which supports R033-06 (form once seen as non-essential) and the late-belief half of R033-09; mild cross-item cueing
R033-01.notes: Passage traces the author's shift from unrhymed accuracy to seeing shape as one of the statements and translating with selective rhyme. A is the author's early view (and the author still keeps 'not at any cost'); B overgeneralizes the reader's letter; D is too narrow.

R033-02.notes: P2 opens 'My reasoning seemed sound' and gives the case against forced rhyme, which the author revises in P4-P5. B overstates; C is P6 (second book); D misplaces P3's review detail.

R033-03.notes: Contrast with 'what the poems say' = content kept, feel/experience lost. A is contradicted ('accurate'); C plays on 'sung by her grandmother'; B is unsupported.

R033-04.notes: 'kept both words and lost the collision' after describing words that sound alike but mean near-opposites. B is a trap directly contradicted ('kept both words'); D is the padding they avoided; C (meter) is not mentioned.

flags: minor: 'chime' also occurs in P2 ('because they chime', a verb), so students may look in the wrong place; the stem's paragraph reference resolves it
minor: C ('a signal of agreement') is somewhat attractive given P4's 'the ear heard agreement', but contrast with 'echo' (near-rhyme) clearly makes B the best answer
R033-05.notes: Near-rhymes are heard 'as an echo rather than a chime', so chime = full, exact sound match. A is the literal-meaning trap; D does not fit the contrast.

flags: minor: overlaps conceptually with R033-01 and R033-09 (all turn on the earlier vs. later view of form)
R033-06.notes: 'happened to come in a pleasing shape' = form was attractive but incidental. A and D contradict 'happened to'; B is not the point of the phrase.

R033-07.notes: Moving rhymes keeps 'the collision' (the effect) while compromising, without the padding of forced exact rhyme. A plays on singing; B is contradicted (form purists say he took too few liberties); C is contradicted by 'near' rhymes and moved rhymes.

R033-08.notes: Followed by 'A translation is a set of losses chosen on purpose': both sides correctly see that something is lost. A, C and D are unsupported.

flags: minor: B closely paraphrases the P5 sentence 'I now think of the shape as one of the statements', which makes it a strong lookup-style trap (only a later belief). That is intended, but it overlaps with R033-06
minor: the evidence that D still holds later is in P5 ('really are as bad as I thought'), not literally 'at the end'; acceptable, but the stem's 'at the end' may make students hunt in P7
R033-09.notes: The P2 belief in padding is reaffirmed in P5. A and C are only early beliefs (abandoned); B is only the later belief. This needs a two-time-point synthesis, and B catches quick readers.
